types.name: DeletedRecord
types.description:
A tombstone for a deleted top-level entity, surfaced by the deletedSince query so sync clients
can reconcile removals incrementally instead of fetching and diffing the entire id set.

types.name: DeletedSinceResult
types.description:
A page of deletion tombstones plus the cursor a client should persist to resume.

Resumability contract: persist `cursor` and pass it back as deletedSince(after:) on the next
poll. Because tombstones are paged by the table's monotonic autoincrement id (not by the
1-second-resolution deleted_at), resuming from a cursor never drops a tombstone written later in
the same wall-clock second. When `pruned` is true the server has discarded tombstones older than
its retention horizon and the caller's cursor predates them, so the caller must full-resync (diff
the entire id set) rather than trust this incremental feed.

types.name: Directory

types.name: EntityChangeEvent
types.description:
NG-only. A metadata-only notification that a tracked top-level entity was created, updated, or
destroyed, delivered over the entityChanged subscription. It mirrors the outbound webhook payload:
kind + id + operation + time ONLY — deliberately NO titles, paths, or other content (privacy + a
small payload). To act on a change, a client refetches the entity by id (or prunes it on destroy).

types.name: ID
types.description: The `ID` scalar type represents a unique identifier, often used to refetch an object or as key for a cache. The ID type appears in a JSON response as a String; however, it is not intended to be human-readable. When expected as an input type, any string (such as "4") or integer (such as 4) input value will be accepted as an ID.

types.name: ServerCapabilities
types.description:
ServerCapabilities lets clients detect the Stash NG fork and which fork-only
features it supports BEFORE invoking them. Original upstream Stash does not
define the serverCapabilities query, so a "Cannot query field" GraphQL error
is the negative signal: clients should treat that error as edition = upstream
and gate all NG-only behaviour off.

types.name: Timestamp
types.description:
Timestamp is a point in time. It is always output as RFC3339-compatible time points.
It can be input as a RFC3339 string, or as "<4h" for "4 hours in the past" or ">5m"
for "5 minutes in the future"
